conceptZh: 要：想要、需要；一隻手特別長的玩具機器人伸長手去拿，最後得到想要的東西。
object: a boxy toy robot built from mismatched parts with one very long arm, reaching for a gigantic lollipop on a high shelf and a tiny teaspoon
morph: a giant lollipop and a tiny spoon force the robot to improvise, and his reaching arm swings the pieces into the glyph 要
creativeAngle: 玩具機器人一隻手特別長，想要的糖果大得離譜、湯匙卻小得可憐，他到處亂想辦法，伸手一撈剛好撈出要字。
promptEn: An 8-second bright, clean toy-animation clip on a solid pale lemon-cream backdrop. Cast: one boxy toy robot built from mismatched parts, a square red body, a round blue head, a tiny yellow foot and one arm much longer than the other, plus one comically oversized swirly lollipop taller than he is. The only text on screen is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 要, drawn in saturated tomato-red strokes, ending centered, uncropped, about 70 percent of frame height with margins. 0.0-1.5s: the robot clanks in, spots a giant swirl lollipop leaning against the wall, and holds up his short arm to point; the lollipop is far too big for his hand and he stands on tiptoe, wobbling. The first narrated 要 lands as he stretches his long arm out in a happy reaching pose and a red stroke flies from his fingertips. 1.5-3.5s: he tries to lift the lollipop with a tiny teaspoon, which flicks the candy into a spin; he tries tugging it with the long arm, which stretches like a spring and snaps back, knocking his own head sideways with a clank. The second narrated 要 lands as the lollipop's swirl unspools into the strokes and clicks into place, completing 要 in the center. 3.5-5.0s: the robot, delighted, hugs the giant lollipop, which pulls him off the ground, and he squeaks into the air with his long arm stretched, then pops down onto his one tiny foot. As the word 我要 is spoken the robot points to his own chest with the short arm and then to the lollipop with the long arm, nodding vigorously. 5.0-8.0s: the glyph is perfectly still and readable for the last 3 seconds while the robot licks the lollipop at a distance with his long arm, bounces on his tiny foot, and his head spins once with happiness, away from the strokes. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin, clear tones, no erhua, reading exactly these syllables: 要、要、我要 (ㄧㄠˋ、ㄧㄠˋ、ㄨㄛˇ ㄧㄠˋ). The character twice with a short pause, then the word once, then stop. The word is audio only. No background music, no extra speech, no subtitles or flashing effects; stylized toy characters only, no real people.
